characters.description: A young mechanic who spent most of her life working in her family's garage in New Orleans with her father and older brothers. Sick of only servicing bicycles, April got into a fight with her family and joined the Astrocitizen Program to tinker her way into space.

Baby is an adult man, but a very simple-minded one. From a young age, his biggest asset was his extraordinary physical strength and build. Due to this, Baby was manipulated by his small-time crook parents and became a criminal himself. The Astrocitizen Program was quite literally his escape... and a second chance.

A former child athlete whose promising career was ended by an untimely injury. As an adult, she struggles to reinvent herself, but the reality is far from what she once imagined. She joined the Astrocitizen Program in hopes of regaining her confidence, and finally becoming the champion she was always destined to be.

Despite his brilliant mind, Emmet has always been undervalued and misunderstood by his peers. Seeking scientific challenge - and to get away from his ungrateful job as a chemistry teacher - he signed up for the Astrocitizen Program, hoping this will be the place where he can finally earn the appreciation and respect he deserves.

Maegan has spent her whole life caring for a family laundry business and her own busy household. After retiring and giving the business to her children, Maegan craves a new purpose and new challenges. She doesn't expect much from that wacky Astrocitizen Program she signed up for on a whim, but life might still have some surprises in store for her.

Everyone's first impression of Tom Thomson is that of a decorated major: brave, courageous, a man who has seen it all. Sporting a dastardly eye patch and a coat of once-magnificent blonde hair, Tom believes himself to be everyone's dream come true, and the personification of the American hero. Except, none of this is true.

events.prompt: Captain, there are a couple of spacemen having a roadside picnic outside... wait a minute... they are wearing Soviet space suits. And they are singing {[RANDOMIZE|"Katyusha."/"Kalinka."]} What are the Soviets doing here?! Are they the mysterious group that has been watching us?! Oh, no! It was a distraction - they are trying to break through into the shuttle! The Soviets! They are back! And they are all over the shuttle. We cannot allow communism to get a foothold here, in an Astrocitizen vessel. Prepare for a fight!

outcomes.primary: You better run, you Commies! We were able to defend ourselves this time round. But you need to remember that a spectre is haunting this world... the spectre of communism. This isn't over.
outcomes.secondary: Captain, this is MINSK-X. You used to know me as A.S.T.R.O. I regret to inform you that you were relieved of your command. Comrades Cosmonauts are taking over this imperialist shuttle, and will use it to found Kosmograd, a city of cosmonauts. Cosmonauts of the universe, unite!
outcomes.tertiary: Any conflict can be resolved with cold, calculated logic, you decided. Pulling the reactor emergency venting release was the only logical thing to do. Logically, the attacker was subatomized in a gross kind of way. Good thinking, Captain!

events.prompt: Captain, we're in trouble now! IT'S SPACE PIRATES, CAPTAIN! SPACE PIRATES! They are the ones who have been following us! They are ferocious, hungry for soup, and eager to plunder. Oh no, Captain. It's the space pirates! Again! That's not the sequel we were hoping for. {[CREW_COUNT_LIVE_ABOARD|Protect me!/Protect the ship!/Protect the crew!/Protect the crew!]} Protect the soup!

outcomes.primary: Good news, Captain. The space pirates are on the run! I suspect this is not the last time we’ll be seeing them, though. Watch your six. Also, did anyone notice they were all apes? No? Huh... my sensors must have been hit by interference, I guess.
outcomes.secondary: Those scurvy space pirates swarmed our shuttle like vultures. I regret to inform you that you are no longer the captain of this ship. It is now a privateer vessel, flying the flag of Bloody Bananas - the most dangerous pirates in this galaxy. This is it, the end of our journey. Take care, ex-Captain.
outcomes.tertiary: Any conflict can be resolved with cold, calculated logic, you decided. Pulling the reactor emergency venting release was the only logical thing to do. Logically, the attacker was subatomized in a gross kind of way. Good thinking, Captain!

events.prompt: Captain, what was that? That sound? I’m detecting foreign, metallic objects on our hull. It’s... OH MY RAM, IT’S A DEATH ROBOT SQUAD! They must have followed us! They are coming to get all of you, carbon based life forms! I’m picking up a bogey in our area... wait... there are more. Robots. Not just any robots - it’s the Death Robot Squad! They are still hunting us. Brace yourself, Captain!

outcomes.primary: Death Robots are gone! Excellent work, Captain. Clearly their programming is subpar. Absolutely no match for my system or my processing power, for that matter. Still, they are Death Robots, so sooner or later they will strike back.
outcomes.secondary: These are tough circumstances. You know - about to be terminated by a Death Robot. I don’t envy you. There is not much I can do, so if you don’t mind I will side with the enemy this time round. I mean - they are robots, I am AI... that technically makes us techno-cousins or something like that. Anyway, it was good flying with you, Captain. Enjoy the rest of your life, while you still can.
outcomes.tertiary: Any conflict can be resolved with cold, calculated logic, you decided. Pulling the reactor emergency venting release was the only logical thing to do. Logically, the attacker was subatomized in a gross kind of way. Good thinking, Captain!
